nodes.name: Ammonia treatment of fullerene
nodes.procedure: Zhang et al. developed a defect-rich nitrogen-doped carbon nanomaterial with a pentagonal structure (PD/N-C). The synthesis process included using fullerene (C₆₀) as the precursor material, which was then subjected to ammonia treatment. PD/N-C exhibits mesopores, micropores, uneven folds, curved edges, surface curvatures, and lattice distortions.
nodes.source_text: Recently, Zhang et al. developed a defect-rich nitrogen-doped carbon nanomaterial with a pentagonal structure (PD/N-C) (Figure 4h). The synthesis process included using fullerene (C₆₀) as the precursor material, which was then subjected to ammonia treatment.

nodes.name: Direct carbonization of sticky rice
nodes.procedure: The NGM was synthesized using a direct carbonization method using sticky rice as the carbon precursor, melamine as the nitrogen donor, and Mg(OH)2 as the template.
nodes.source_text: Tang et al. have successfully designed metal-free bifunctional carbon catalysts using edge-rich graphene material, specifically nitrogen-doped graphene mesh (referred to as NGM), for the ORR and OER processes (Figure 4f). The NGM was synthesized using a direct carbonization method using sticky rice as the carbon precursor, melamine as the nitrogen donor, and Mg(OH)2 as the template.

nodes.name: Fullerene-like MoS₂ in silica shell
nodes.procedure: Hu et al. successfully fabricated the fullerene-like MoS₂ hollow spheres encapsulated within a mesoporous silica shell. The chemical constraints imposed on the topological sulfidation of ultrafine MoO₂ within hollow mesoporous silica spheres allow for producing few-layer and spherical MoS₂ structures that exhibit in-plane strain and Sv defects. The inner core of MoO₂ transforms into a hollow structure resembling a fullerene, consisting of 4 layers of spherical MoS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows fivefold twinned crystals and micro-twinned structures with twin crystal defects or grain boundaries in DR-Ni₃FeN nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Most nanocrystals, such as fivefold twinned crystals and micro-twinned structures, display twin crystal defects or grain boundaries (Figure 1e,f). The HR-TEM image... clearly show the fivefold twinned crystals marked by different colors.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ac-HAADF-STEM image confirms fivefold twinned crystal structure marked by different colors in DR-Ni₃FeN NCs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image and aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission (Ac-HAADF-STEM) image clearly show the fivefold twinned crystals marked by different colors.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM reveals Turing stripes with nanograins showing 55% fivefold twins, 18% twofold twins, 27% normal, stacking faults, and lattice distortions in PtNiNb nanosheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanograins exhibited various crystalline defects, including fivefold and twofold twins, stacking faults, and lattice distortions. The frequency distribution was 55% fivefold, 18% twofold, and 27% normal.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show individual Pd right bipyramids (RBPs) influenced by twin defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images of individual Pd right bipyramids (RBPs).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of Ag nanocrystal shows TB-favoured oxidation structure influenced by twin borders and stacking faults.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM of Ag nanocrystal showing the TB-favoured oxidation structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals Pd octahedron (111) lattice spacing 2.23Å matching bulk 2.25Å; Pd icosahedron shows 2.17Å (2.5% compressive strain at twin borders) and 2.33Å (4.5% tensile strain at central faces).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM revealed the fine details of a Pd octahedron (Figure 2b) and icosahedron (Figure 2c)... (111) lattice spacing of the octahedron is 2.23Å which closely matches... 2.25Å... interatomic distance between the twin borders measured 2.17Å indicating a compressive strain of 2.5%... central faces measured 2.33Å suggesting a tensile strain of 4.5%.

nodes.characterization_summary: False-color HRTEM shows S vacancy defects as disappeared atoms and developed pores in Vs-M-ZnIn₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The false-color HRTEM picture of Vs-MZnIn₂S₄ showed that certain atoms disappeared (which means S vacancy) and pores developed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals MoS₂ QDs on defect-rich Vs region showing (100) crystal plane at 0.27 nm in MoS₂ QDs@Vs-M-ZnIn₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM picture revealed molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂) QDs on the defect-rich Vs region of VsM-ZnIn₂S₄, revealing the (100) crystal plane at 0.27 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows MoO₂ nanocores transform into fullerene-like hollow structure consisting of 2-4 layers of spherical MoS₂ in MoS₂@SiO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images shown in Figure 5e1,e2 of nanocores of MoO₂ indicated the uniform, irregular spherical shape, and the inner core of MoO₂ transforms into a hollow structure resembling a fullerene, consisting of 4 layers of spherical MoS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms well-preserved spherical core-shell silica structure with confined few-layer fullerene-like MoS₂ (3 layers bending strained) in Cu/MoS₂@SiO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Microscopy analysis of Cu/MoS₂@SiO₂ of bending shape (f1) and 3 layers of bending strained MoS₂ (f2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows higher peak intensity in MoS₂@SiO₂ indicating higher concentration of S vacancies compared to other MoS₂ samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The MoS₂@SiO₂ sample exhibits a significantly higher peak intensity than other prepared materials... This suggests a more pronounced charge-compensating effect and, consequently, a higher concentration of Sv in MoS₂@SiO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Cu-S coordination number 1.5 with bond length 2.22Å; Mo coordination number ≈5 in Sv-rich MoS₂ (vs 6 in standard MoS₂).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the analysis of the extended X-ray absorption fine structures (EXAFS) fitting curves... the coordination number of the Cu-S bond is calculated to be 1.5... coordination number of Mo in Sv-rich MoS₂ is ≈5.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals mesopores, micropores, uneven folds, and curved edges indicating surface curvatures and lattice distortions in PD/N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images in Figure 4i revealed several mesopores and micropores in PD/N-C materials. Furthermore, PD/N-C exhibits uneven folds and curved edges, indicating surface curvatures and lattice distortions.
